              File status by Publisher

              Normalized publisher names (variants merged), broken down by file status like the institution chart above. Only publishers with at least 100 publications in the current selection. “No publisher” and “Other publisher” (long tail, not normalized) are excluded here. Shows absolute counts, sorted by total publications, by default — use the controls above to switch to percentages or a different sort.

              File status is determined per publication: "Open file" if at least one file is publicly accessible (COAR c_abf2), otherwise "Embargoed file" if files exist but are all embargoed (c_f1cf), otherwise "No file". License is the first license of the first file; where file or license information is missing, this is shown separately. "Unknown" for open access status means: no ar:Access value in the source metadata. Publisher is the first name from cerif:Publishers, with common spelling variants (e.g. "Elsevier B.V.", "Elsevier Inc.", "Elsevier Ltd") merged into a single name; publications with no publisher field fall under "No publisher", less frequent publishers under "Other publisher". "OA Switchboard partner" uses that same first publisher name, matched by substring against the OA Switchboard participant list (checked 1 Oct 2026); it is independent of the Publisher bucketing above and may classify some long-tail publishers as a match even though they aren't broken out individually elsewhere in the dashboard.

              Source: DURF Full Text Monitor · static snapshot of the SURF ORI DuckLake catalog (cris.publications, loaded 4 March 2026) · open the interactive dashboard for filters and the queries behind the figures.

              Embed this chart

              Paste this snippet into any web page (a CMS “HTML” block, a Markdown page, a blog post). It shows just this chart from the full dataset, with its current %/# setting and sort order, and links back to this dashboard. The sidebar filters are not carried over.

              The embedded page also reports its height to the host page (postMessage with type: "durf-embed-height"), so a page that listens for it can size the iframe exactly; otherwise the height in the snippet is used. A host page can switch the embed to its own light/dark theme with postMessage({type: "durf-embed-theme", theme: "dark"}).

              Preview

              Background & data currency

              DURF Theme 3: Full Text Capture

              This dashboard is a direct outcome of DURF (Dutch Repository Federation), Theme 3 – Full Text Capture. See the full roadmap on the DURF Gantt chart. It was built following discussions with the Theme leads for Theme 3 and Theme 2, Pascal and Rutger.

              Goal

              • Comprehensive full-text availability in Dutch repository/CRIS systems, primarily to enhance preservation, and secondarily to enable text-mining, AI usage, and Taverne mechanisms.
              • Establish baseline metrics and a reporting system for full-text uptake.

              Outcome

              • A Digital Sovereignty Health CRIS/Repo Dashboard: a chart with the ratio of metadata records containing a link to a file (PDF) on the institutional domain, per repository, over time.
              Proof of concept, not a live connection: this dashboard does not query the DuckLake catalog live. Every figure was fetched once via a direct DuckDB connection to the public SURF ORI DuckLake catalog and embedded in this page as a static snapshot. If new data lands in the catalog afterwards — institutions depositing files, harvests re-running, metadata edits — none of that will appear here. The numbers will drift from the live catalog over time; treat this as a demonstration of what's possible, not a monitoring tool, until it's wired up to refresh automatically or rebuilt from a fresh extract.
              Data currency: the cris.publications table in this catalog was last (re)loaded on 4 March 2026 (UTC, per the catalog's own snapshot log). Individual records also carry their own last-modified timestamp from the source repository (OAI-PMH header.datestamp), which ranges up to 15 April 2026 depending on the institution — see per-institution dates . Everything in this dashboard is a static snapshot as of those dates: if an institution deposits files, changes access rights, or otherwise edits records afterwards, that will not show up here until the catalog is reloaded and this dashboard is rebuilt from it.

              OA Switchboard exploration: the “Only publishers reachable via OA Switchboard” switch and the manual-capture-cost KPI/chart under Exploratory analysis are a first pass at a cost–benefit case for whether OA Switchboard could build a service to help CRIS/repositories capture PDFs from its partner publishers. The switch matches the first publisher name on a record against OA Switchboard's published participant list (live + preparing to go live, checked 1 Oct 2026) by case-insensitive substring — approximate, same caveat as the dashboard's other publisher normalization. The 7-minutes-per-record manual-capture estimate comes from one institution's own figures from their 2023 Taverne retro-opt-out exercise (~450 journal articles ≈ 52 hours); it hasn't been validated for other institutions or publication types — book chapters, in particular, are reported anecdotally to take noticeably longer per record than journal articles. Use the publication-type filter to scope the cost estimate to the types this rate actually reflects.

              Source: SURF ORI DuckLake, schema cris.publications. Data aggregated by institution × publication type × year × open access status × file status × license × publisher × OA Switchboard match. Years 1995–2025 (2026 is still in progress).
